216.summary: Careful consent and expiry terms for a 7-day road-alert pass, with honest safety limits. The description quotes a 0.001 USD-TDN payment while the price is 0.50, and says the item stays inactive while it is listed publicly. No privacy link for the WhatsApp number it serves.

215.summary: Self-described test item that grants no access, still public in the catalog.

207.summary: Free, deterministic opportunity-match score (0 to 100, with reasons) for students, in Spanish, with a well-described schema. No llms.txt and no feedback item.

203.summary: Sold at 5 USD-TDN with an empty description: nothing says what a buyer gets, for how long, or how refunds work.

201.summary: Free daily look at the Newsroom briefing before buying, with a not-advice line and a read-me covering errors and expected misses.

202.summary: Free feedback and refund route with a reference id, an optional transaction id and a privacy link for the reply email.

200.summary: Free rating lookup by item number, with a free direct URL for bulk use, an explicit not-advice line and unrated items answered 200 ok:false.

212.summary: Hackathon demo, clearly labelled synthetic and not a real charity. Our own records show it points at the same test service as #213, so it may not return the receipt it describes; not yet checked by a live call. No read-me link; open schema with an unbounded sponsor name on a paid item.

213.summary: Checked by a live paid call on 18 Oct: the item answers from a test service that echoes the request back. No officer approval and no water-point receipt, which the listing promises. Labelled a hackathon demo.

214.summary: Hackathon demo that takes a committee water report and says plainly it never shows water is safe to drink. Takes a phone number with no privacy link; open schema; no read-me link.
